full_judgment:
Mustafa Kama J: This petition for leave to appeal by the plaintiff-petitioner is from the judgment and order dated 16-3-97 passed by a learned Single Judge of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 598 of 1989 making the Rule absolute, setting aside the appellate judgment and decree dated 16-5-89 passed by the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka which decreed the suit in Title Appeal No. 29 of 1984, after setting aside the judgment and decree dated 12-12-83 passed by the trial Court, the 1st Court of Munsif, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 670 of 1977 which dismissed the suit. 

 2. The suit was for a declaration that the plaintiff-petitioner is the absolute owner of the suit land and also for permanent injunction. Both the plaintiff-petitioner and the defendant respondents agreed that the suit property originally belonged to Jogesh Chandra Saha and others who transferred the same by registered kabala dated 6-9-55 to four brothers, namely, Salimuddin, Hafizuddin, Aminuddin and Afsaruddin. Both sides assert that the four brothers enjoyed specific portions of their purchased land out of his own share of land by amicable partition. It is the plaintiff-petitioner's case that Salimuddin entered into an agreement for sale of 0.81 acres of land to one Asiruddin Choudhury. On Salimuddin's failure to register a deed of sale Asiruddin Chowdhury filed a suit for specific performance of contract which was decreed. Asiruddin after obtaining kabala from court sold 0.13 acres of land out of 0.81 acres of land in CS plot No. 42 to the plaintiff. The defendant-respondents case is that the same suit land comprising an area of 0.13 acres fell in the exclusive saham of Afsaruddin, another brother of Salimuddin. The defendants purchased the said 0.13 acres of land from Afsaruddin on 27-5-66. Both sides claimed mutation, possession and payment of rent. 

 4. The lower appellate Court found that the plaintiff purchased 0.13 acres of land with specific boundaries and the purchased deed attracts the suit property. The defendant has no right, title and possession in the suit property. As such the suit was decreed. 

 5. The High Court Division found that neither the plaintiff nor the defendant could prove that suit plot No. 42 was amicably partitioned either between the four co-sharers or between the plaintiff and the defendants. As such it is not physically possible to give a decree for declaration of title to a definite portion of the land in CS Plot No. 42. The appellate Court below committed an error of law in decreeing the suit in the absence of partition by metes and bounds of the land in CS plot No. 42.
